findings.title: ⌘F1 ribbon toggle removed on macOS even though the PR says it still works, and the regression script was edited to hide it
findings.failure: The old binding was `mod+f1`, which is ⌘F1 on a Mac. The new list is `Key::windows("ctrl+f1")` and `Key::mac("cmd+alt+r")`, so on macOS ⌘F1 is no longer bound. A Mac user who presses ⌘F1 sees nothing happen, but the PR description says "⌘F1 still works". The plan requires e2e/ribbon.sh to pass unchanged, yet e2e/scripts/fude-commands.json had its ⌘F1 presses (t=2.30/2.50) swapped for ⌥⌘R. That is why the existing collapse/expand checks still pass and the lost binding goes unnoticed. Either add `Key::mac("cmd+f1")` after ⌥⌘R, or correct the description and restore the original script.

findings.title: Windows zoom-in tooltip check always passes
findings.failure: The loop runs `grep -qF '"Vergrößern"'` on the tree. The zoom-in node always has `"label": "Vergrößern"`, so the grep matches even when `help` is "Vergrößern (Strg++)" or "Vergrößern (Strg+=)". The check cannot detect a Windows zoom shortcut leaking into the tooltip, yet it is logged as `PASS tooltip (windows): Vergrößern`. It should match the help field, e.g. `"help": "Vergrößern"`.

suggestion.code:
for tip in "Wiederholen (Strg+Y)" "Menüband ein- oder ausblenden (Strg+F1)" "Vergrößern"; do
  if grep -qF "\"help\": \"$tip\"" "$tmp/tooltips-win.json"; then echo "PASS tooltip (windows): $tip" | tee -a "$log"; else echo "FAIL tooltip (windows): $tip" | tee -a "$log"; fail=1; fi
done
